text:
incident-bot: Pager: elevated 429s on hosted /v1/embeddings in us-west (P2) at 1999998888. Observed ~6% 429s over last 10m. Runbook: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/embeddings-429

incident-bot: Alert details: spike started ~1999998600, affected batcher pool embeddings-batcher-1, autoscale not reacting fast enough.

maria: I'm the current primary, jumping on bridge now. Jamal can you be secondary? I'll own customer comms and mitigation coordination.

jamal: Joining bridge. I'll handle infra scaling and canary rollback if needed.

alex: Quick check: embeddings-batcher-1 showing backlog and CPU saturation on worker nodes (avgCPU 89-95%). Latency p95 up, not memory.

prod-support: CS: multiple customers reporting failures. Opening status page entry now. Will notify affected enterprise reps.

maria: Plan: (1) scale up worker replicas in us-west, (2) roll back recent batcher canary if backlog persists, (3) toggle prefix cache as a quick mitigation per runbook, (4) route low-priority traffic to CPU fallback. Jamal + Alex coordinate infra steps.

jamal: Executing scale and rollout restart:
```
kubectl -n inference scale deploy/embeddings-worker --replicas=9 -l region=us-west
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/embeddings-batcher-1
```
Scaling kicked off, pods creating.

jamal: Attempting canary rollback to image tag v2.3.2 from v2.3.5 for batcher.

alex: Toggling prefix-cache off to see effect (runbook step):
```
redis-cli -h redis-us-west set embeddings:prefix_cache:enabled 0
```
Turning off prefix cache now.

maria: prod-support please post a short status: "Investigating increased 429s for embeddings in US-West. Engineers are mitigating; updates in 15 minutes."

prod-support: Posted to status.redwood.com under "embeddings degraded". Included ETA and note that enterprise customers were notified. :loud_sound: 

jamal: New pods started but one failed readiness — checking init logs.

alex: Init failure root cause: KMS startup probe timeouts hitting during pod init (kube-dns lookup delays). Restarting pod helped one replica. Adding probe retry logs to ticket.

maria: Status check: after scale + rollback + cache toggle error rate dropped from ~6% to ~2.3% over 6 minutes. Still seeing intermittent spikes on high-concurrency traffic.

jamal: Next action: enable CPU fallback path for low-priority requests and mark a portion of non-SLA traffic to fallback. That should stop 429s for bursty low-priority workloads.

alex: Enabling CPU fallback via routing flag:
```
curl -s -X POST "https://routing-api.internal/flags" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"region":"us-west","embeddings_cpu_fallback":true}'
```
Flag applied, routing shows ~20% of requests now taking fallback path. Monitoring.

prod-support: CS update posted: noted fallback routing for low-priority jobs; high-priority customers still on GPU path. We're sending targeted updates to the three affected enterprise contacts.

maria: Operational summary for handoff: primary=maria -> switching to jamal shortly, secondary=jamal now, infra lead=alex, cs=prod-support. Mitigations applied: workers scaled, batcher rolled back, prefix-cache off, CPU fallback enabled. Error rate trending down ~1.8% last 5m.

jamal: I'll keep an eye on synthetic load tests for high-concurrency users. Also adding temporary emergency autoscale rule for embeddings-workers to avoid re-occurrence this hour.

alex: I'll open an internal ticket to diff batcher config between v2.3.2 and v2.3.5 and attach logs. Also escalate KMS probe flakiness to infra/kms team.

maria: Post-incident actions: (A) keep scaled replicas for 2 hours, (B) schedule RCA focused on batcher queueing + recent config change, (C) follow up with DNS/KMS for probe timing, (D) update runbook with a KMS-init checklist. Postmortem owner: alex (will draft).

jamal: Confirming takeover: I'll be primary at 2000003600. I'll monitor and open runbook PR for probe retry guidance.

prod-support: CS closed interim loop with affected customers; they'll reopen if they see more issues.

oncall-bot: Reminder: file incident report in #incidents within 24h. Include timeline, impact, mitigations, and follow-ups.

maria: Leaving bridge in 30m. Handing off to jamal as primary. Final note: initial alert -> mitigations within ~12 minutes; residual error rate <2% and decreasing. Incident artifact: https://redwood-internal/incidents/1999998888

jamal: Ack, taking over at 2000003600. Will post morning status update and follow up on autoscale tuning. :thumbsup:
